entries.name: Anecoop
entries.heading: Anecoop and the Moscatel Tradition of Valencia
paragraphs: Anecoop, rooted in Valencia since its founding in 1975, is not a typical winery but a vast agricultural cooperative that now coordinates the work of some 61 member cooperatives and over 20,000 farmers across Spain. While best known globally for citrus and fresh produce, the group also oversees a wine division that connects growers to markets with a foundation in tradition, innovation, and respect for place. Anecoop Bodegas operates within this structure, aligning winemaking with the cooperative’s sustainability and quality values. (Sources: Anecoop corporate site; LinkedIn overview)

Valencia’s Denominación de Origen Protegida plays a central role in ensuring the authenticity and character of the region’s wines, particularly its renowned Moscatel offerings. The DO comprises four distinct subzones, including the Moscatel zone where vineyards typically lie at up to 200 meters altitude near the Mediterranean. This area is celebrated for producing aromatic liquor-style Moscatel wines and is subject to strict regulated standards, such as an alcohol minimum of 15%, ensuring typicity and quality. These controls support producers like Anecoop in reliably delivering varietally expressive Moscatel wines from Valencia. (Sources: DO Valencia Regulatory Board; Comunidad Valenciana gastronomic guide)

entries.name: Bianchi
entries.heading: Bianchi of Piedmont: Erbaluce and Nebbiolo from Canavese and Ghemme
paragraphs: Bianchi, based in Sizzano in Alto Piemonte, works intimately with two emblematic Piedmont grape varieties. Their white wine comes from Erbaluce, an ancient variety rooted in the Canavese area around Caluso and the moraine hills of Ivrea. This variety is appreciated for its vitality, crisp acidity and capacity to take on forms ranging from still whites to sparkling and passito wines. Erbaluce di Caluso achieved DOCG status in 2010, underscoring its importance to the region.([piemonteland.it](https://www.piemonteland.it/vini/erbaluce/?utm_source=openai)) Bianchi’s red wine focuses on Nebbiolo from the Ghemme DOCG, where Nebbiolo has long been esteemed for producing structured, ageworthy wines that carry the region’s mineral and elegant signature.([cantinabianchi.it](https://www.cantinabianchi.it/i-nostri-vini?utm_source=openai))

In both expressions Bianchi captures the geological and historical spirit of Alto Piemonte. The Erbaluce, grown in morainic soils with sharp, glacial origins, delivers fresh, fragrant whites that reflect the terroir’s minerality and tradition.([erbalu.it](https://www.erbalu.it/territory/?lang=en&utm_source=openai)) Meanwhile, the Nebbiolo of Ghemme draws on the region’s rugged hills and historic DOCG framework to yield red wines of depth, structure and a poised personality.([cantinabianchi.it](https://www.cantinabianchi.it/i-nostri-vini?utm_source=openai)) Whether for lively white or textured red, Bianchi offers expressions firmly anchored in Piedmont’s heritage, inviting buyers to explore these regional signatures in their portfolio.

entries.name: Coastal Ridge
entries.heading: Coastal Ridge: California’s Accessible Wine Offering
paragraphs: Coastal Ridge is a producer rooted in California whose wines span several of the state’s most familiar and widely planted varietals. Their range includes Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Merlot, Pinot Noir, and White Zinfandel. While the winery’s own official web presence appears limited, third‑party retail and listings confirm these varietals are accurately represented in their portfolio ([cpdwineliquor.com](https://cpdwineliquor.com/collections/coastal-ridge?utm_source=openai)). These grapes are among California’s most significant both in terms of acreage and consumer recognition. Notably, Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon together accounted for more than one‑third of all tonnage crushed in California in 2024, while Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir, Zinfandel, Chardonnay, and Merlot consistently rank among the state’s leading varieties ([ers.usda.gov](https://www.ers.usda.gov/data-products/charts-of-note/111472?utm_source=openai)).

For a wine buyer, Coastal Ridge offers approachable expressions of key California styles. Cabernet Sauvignon often displays ripe black‑fruit flavors and moderate tannins, Chardonnay leans toward fruit‑driven with balanced structure, Merlot tends to be supple and fruit‑forward, and Pinot Noir and White Zinfandel provide lighter, easy‑drinking options. These styles align with consumer familiarity and versatility across a range of food pairings, making Coastal Ridge a practical choice for both everyday menus and broader selections.

entries.name: Collotte
entries.eyebrow: Domaine Collotte of Côte de Nuits
entries.heading: Isabelle and Philippe Collotte in Burgundy’s northern Côte de Nuits
paragraphs: In the cool, limestone-rich hills of the northern Côte de Nuits, Domaine Collotte embodies quiet precision and a deep respect for each vineyard. Operated by Philippe Collotte, who took over the family’s small estate in 1981 and has been joined since 2014 by his daughter Isabelle, the domaine now spans approximately sixteen hectares around Marsannay‑la‑Côte with holdings extending into Fixin, Gevrey‑Chambertin and Chambolle‑Musigny ([caves-carriere.fr](https://www.caves-carriere.fr/en/1935-collotte?utm_source=openai)). The Collottes cultivate their vines with care, eschewing chemical herbicides in favor of plowing and low yields, achieving High Environmental Quality certification while seeking to let each terroir speak for itself ([domainecollotte.com](https://domainecollotte.com/notre-savoir-faire/?utm_source=openai)).

Their range includes white wines from Chardonnay and red wines from Pinot Noir, with styles shaped by gentle vinification and measured aging to emphasize clarity, finesse and the personality of each parcel ([domainecollotte.com](https://domainecollotte.com/en/our-wines/?utm_source=openai)). The family's approach consistently places the spotlight on expression rather than manipulation. For wine buyers exploring the FineVines portfolio, Collotte offers a compelling journey through Marsannay, Fixin, and Gevrey‑Chambertin terroirs, in both red and white, anchored by a legacy of thoughtful stewardship and terroir-focused expression.

entries.name: Comtadine
entries.heading: Comtadine’s Provençal Heart in Grenache-driven Côtes du Rhône
paragraphs: Comtadine is not an individual estate but the historic Cave La Comtadine, a cooperative cellar founded in 1930 in Puyméras, in the southern Rhône. Today it brings together over 280 growers cultivating some 1 300 hectares across twenty communes in the Haut‑Vaucluse and Drôme provençale. It produces wines in appellations such as Côtes‑du‑Rhône, Côtes‑du‑Rhône Villages Puyméras and Ventoux, reflecting the terroir’s sun-warmed character and Mediterranean influence. ([vins-rhone-tourisme.fr](https://www.vins-rhone-tourisme.fr/fr/visiter-et-deguster/visite-des-domaines/cave-la-comtadine?utm_source=openai))

The Grenache grape is central to the style of the southern Rhône. It is the region’s most widely planted variety and thrives in its warm, dry climate and varied soils. Its wines are typically generous, round, and fruity, with good weight on the palate and the capacity to reflect local garrigue aromas. In the southern Rhône, Grenache is often blended with varieties like Syrah, Mourvèdre, Carignan and Cinsault, though single‑varietal bottlings are not uncommon, especially in cooperatives such as Comtadine. ([vins-rhone.com](https://www.vins-rhone.com/en/grenache-noir-grape-variety?utm_source=openai))

entries.name: Dashe
entries.heading: Dashe Cellars: Artful, Vineyard-Driven Wines from California
paragraphs: Since their founding in 1996, Michael and Anne Dashe have pursued a terroir‑focused style in California winemaking. Drawing on Anne’s training in Bordeaux and Michael’s years at Ridge and other respected wineries, the couple sources fruit from older‑vine hillside sites with low yields and sustainable practices throughout Sonoma and Mendocino. Their winemaking emphasizes native yeast fermentation and minimal intervention, aiming to express the vineyard in each wine rather than winemaking flair ([dashecellars.com](https://www.dashecellars.com/assets/upload/history-April2020.pdf?utm_source=openai)).

Dashe Cellars’ portfolio bridges the signature single‑vineyard bottlings with their lighter “Les Enfants Terribles” expressions, which often employ carbonic maceration for a more playful, youthfully vibrant character. Their Carignane, for example, is sourced from an 1890‑planted vineyard in the Sacramento River Delta, showcasing how historical vine plantings align with the Dashes’ philosophy of authenticity and sense of place ([dashecellars.com](https://www.dashecellars.com/news/408?utm_source=openai)).

entries.name: Disznoko
entries.heading: Disznókő and the Noble Furmint of Tokaj
paragraphs: Disznókő is a historic and respected estate perched at the gateway to Hungary’s Tokaj region, known for its expressive wines crafted across a spectrum from dry whites to botrytized treasures. The estate revitalized the traditions of Tokaji Aszú beginning in the early 1990s with an approach that balances purity of fruit and the complex character imparted by noble rot. Their winemaking ethos emphasizes deep understanding of site and terroir, reflected in a portfolio ranging from clarity-driven dry wines to the most layered expressions of late-harvest and Aszú style wines ([disznoko.hu](https://disznoko.hu/hu/borkeszites?utm_source=openai)).

Furmint is the cornerstone white grape of Tokaj, celebrated for its high natural acidity, mineral clarity, and remarkable versatility. This variety underpins both vibrant, terroir-driven dry whites and the lush, age-worthy sweet wines of Tokaji Aszú. Furmint’s ability to retain crisp acidity even in richly botrytized wines gives it structure and longevity. The style might vary from green apple, pear and quince in dry bottlings to apricot, honey and ginger in dessert styles, often with compelling minerality derived from Tokaj’s volcanic soils ([bor.hu](https://bor.hu/en/furmint/?utm_source=openai)).

entries.name: Guidi
entries.heading: Guidi of Chianti Classico: Legacy and Expression
paragraphs: Since 1929 the Guidi family has tended vineyards between Siena and Florence, preserving four generations of family craftsmanship in the Chianti Classico zone of Tuscany ([chianticlassico.com](https://www.chianticlassico.com/en/estates/guidi-1929/?utm_source=openai)). Their vineyards in San Donato in Poggio rest on galestro, alberese, and marl soils, ideally suited to Sangiovese’s structure and aromatic depth ([guidi1929.com](https://www.guidi1929.com/en/vineyards/?utm_source=openai)). Today Avio Guidi and his sons maintain this heritage, guided by a rooted respect for their land, ethical farming, and sustainable stewardship ([guidi1929.com](https://www.guidi1929.com/en/?utm_source=openai)).

Chianti Classico itself is one of the most celebrated and tightly defined appellations in the world, with rules that emphasize Sangiovese as the core of the blend, aged with care and authenticity ([chianti.guide](https://chianti.guide/wineries.html?utm_source=openai)). Sangiovese is the emblematic grape of Tuscany and Chianti in particular, celebrated for its ability to convey regional character while aging gracefully ([consorziovinimaremma.it](https://www.consorziovinimaremma.it/en/vines/sangiovese/?utm_source=openai)). Guidi’s focus on Chianti Classico DOCG, responsibly farmed and rooted in tradition, offers a refined, terroir-driven expression of Sangiovese for the FineVines portfolio.

entries.heading: Héritiers du Comte Lafon in the Mâconnais
paragraphs: Héritiers du Comte Lafon is the project of Dominique Lafon, celebrated for his Meursault domain, who in 1999 turned his attention to the Mâconnais, convinced of the unique quality of its limestone-rich southern Burgundy terroirs. The estate holds parcels in Milly‑Lamartine, Bussières, the village of Chardonnay, and the Viré‑Clessé area, including the Clos de la Crochette on calcareous soils that suit Chardonnay exceptionally well ([vistavin.fr](https://www.vistavin.fr/fr/1085-heritiers-comte-lafon?utm_source=openai)). A recent feature noted that wines like those from the Héritiers du Comte Lafon in Le Monsard deliver a denser, riper expression than typical for the region ([decanter.com](https://www.decanter.com/wine/burgundy-wine/decoding-the-maconnais-burgundy-lovers-should-keep-their-eyes-on-this-southern-star?utm_source=openai)).

The Mâconnais is the most southern and one of the largest wine subregions of Burgundy, extending about 35 km between Sennecey‑le‑Grand and Saint‑Vérand, trapped between the valleys of the Grosne and the Saône ([macon-tourisme.com](https://www.macon-tourisme.com/nos-essentiels/les-vignobles-du-maconnais-et-du-beaujolais/le-vignoble-maconnais/?utm_source=openai)). Chardonnay is overwhelmingly dominant here, planted over roughly 80 percent of the vineyards, where calcareous, marly, and siliceous soils impart both finesse and depth and support both approachable and ageworthy styles ([vins-bourgogne.fr](https://www.vins-bourgogne.fr/vins-et-terroirs/notre-vignoble/maconnais/le-maconnais-la-porte-sud-de-la-bourgogne%2C2390%2C9310.html?utm_source=openai)).

entries.heading: Lacroix’s Paul Lacroix Pinot Noir as Vin de France
paragraphs: Lacroix’s Paul Lacroix Pinot Noir Vin de France comes from a tradition of Burgundian family producers, yet its Vin de France designation sets it apart from appellation‑controlled wines. Unlike IGP or AOP (Appellation d’Origine Protégée) that define production zones and strict vineyard practices, Vin de France is the broadest category in the modern French classification. Introduced in 2009, it allows producers flexibility in sourcing and blending grapes while still indicating varietal and vintage on the label ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vin_de_France?utm_source=openai)).

This freedom makes Vin de France a compelling canvas for producers like Lacroix to express creativity and stylistic intent without geographic constraints. While the producer’s Burgundian roots may influence the house style, the Vin de France label primarily communicates that this wine offers approachable Pinot Noir driven by varietal character and vintage expression rather than terroir specification. It complements FineVines’ portfolio by offering buyers a straightforward yet authentic French Pinot Noir representing both tradition and imaginative production.

paragraphs: Nestled in the esteemed village of Le Mesnil‑sur‑Oger on the Côte des Blancs, Launois is a family estate where Chardonnay reigns. The result is a focused expression of limestone‑rich terroir that typifies this segment of Champagne.

Under the Paul Launois label, Julien and Sarah Launois harness a roughly six‑hectare vineyard in Le Mesnil‑sur‑Oger to craft pure Blanc de Blancs Grand Cru. Their Monochrome bottlings, from the eponymous cuvée, are vinified as Extra Brut with minimal dosage, aimed at showcasing vibrant mineral tension and refined texture. This approach accentuates chalk‑driven salinity and delicate Chardonnay character, offering both clarity and personality from a single origin ([sanks.fr](https://sanks.fr/producteurs/champagne-paul-launois?utm_source=openai)).

paragraphs: McNab Ridge Winery stands as a family-rooted producer in Mendocino County, California, with a legacy tracing back to Adolph Parducci, the region’s earliest winemaking pioneer. The family’s approach emphasizes complexity and food‑friendliness, shaping balanced, approachable styles from Mendocino’s diverse terroir. Rich continues to source fruit widely across the county, embracing sustainable practices and drawing on deep generational expertise. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Parducci?utm_source=openai))

Within FineVines’ current selection, the McNab Ridge offerings reflect this philosophy in action. Fred’s Red is a savory, crowd‑pleasing red blend that speaks to the winery’s accessible side. Meanwhile, the Zinzilla Zinfandel showcases the region’s hallmark expressive fruit and structure. Both selections embody the winery’s commitment to crafting balanced, flavorful wines that resonate with everyday enjoyment and reflect the character of Mendocino County. entries.heading: Mont Hermon from the Galilee: Crafted by Golan Heights Winery
paragraphs: Mont Hermon wines are produced by Golan Heights Winery using grapes grown at the foot of Mount Hermon in Israel’s Galilee, a region celebrated for its elevation, volcanic soils, and sharp diurnal temperature shifts that favor complexity and freshness in wine ([fr.wikipedia.org](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mont_Hermon?utm_source=openai)). This setting lends structural clarity and aromatic lift to the wines, and those familiar with the vineyard mosaic in the Golan know that cooler, well‑drained sites like Hermon can yield lively expressions even from Mediterranean red varieties. That heritage gives context to the Syrah‑Tempranillo blend represented in this collection.

Syrah and Tempranillo are both well‑adapted to warm‑climate sites yet benefit from the Galilean terroir’s cooling influences, where higher altitude and volcanic soils support expressive fruit and balanced structure. While Tempranillo brings bright cherry and subtle earth, Syrah contributes savory spice and medium‑bodied depth; the union often yields approachable wines that resonate with both classic and New World styles. FineVines’ selection from Mont Hermon showcases both the distinct identity of that terroir and the flexibility of this varietal pairing for a range of cellar and table contexts.

entries.heading: Nessa: Albariño from Rías Baixas
paragraphs: Nestled within Spain’s northwest region of Galicia, the Rías Baixas appellation is especially acclaimed for its Albariño wines crafted under the regulation and quality oversight of its Consejo Regulador. This denominación de origen, formally established in 1988, spans several coastal sub‑zones and protects the production of Albariño as a varietal, requiring it to reflect the distinctive maritime climate and slate soils of the area ([boe.es](https://www.boe.es/buscar/doc.php?id=BOE-A-1988-19043&utm_source=openai)). Producers in Rías Baixas must adhere to strict standards for vineyard siting, varietal purity, and both analytical and organoleptic controls to carry the DO seal ([boe.es](https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2009-17064&utm_source=openai)).

Within this storied region, Nessa produces a focused expression of Albariño that reflects both the grape’s lineage and the area’s character. While catalog specifics such as vintages or stock levels shift regularly, FineVines' inclusion of Nessa highlights its commitment to Galician whites rooted in place and tradition. A wine buyer exploring this selection can expect a wine that embodies the bright acidity, aroma profile, and mineral vitality typical of Albariño from Rías Baixas, supported by the DO's certification structure without naming particular wines or vintages.

entries.name: Olivier
entries.heading: Olivier of Bergerac: Merlot and Cabernet Franc in Context
paragraphs: Bergerac, in the Dordogne of southwestern France, is one of the oldest appellations, earning its AOC status in 1936. Spread across roughly ninety communes, it sits just east of Bordeaux and features a patchwork of alluvial terraces, clay‑limestone and gravel soils, all shaped by the cool influence of the Dordogne River. This terroir yields wines with balanced ripeness, refined structure and textured fruit expression. The region’s red blends commonly combine Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon, with Merlot often dominant for its plushness and early ripening, while Cabernet Franc brings lifting freshness, floral perfume and clarity to the mix. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bergerac_wine?utm_source=openai))

Understanding Olivier’s Merlot‑Cabernet Franc blend benefits from this regional backdrop. In Bergerac, Merlot tends to deliver smooth, rounded texture and ripe red‑fruit character; Cabernet Franc contributes fine aromatics, structural finesse and a hint of pepper or violet. This complementary pairing reflects the balance that local winemakers seek. The specific expression of Olivier will derive from parcel selection, percentage of each grape, and maturation choices. Within this fine regional context, a single‑wine presentation like Olivier’s fits squarely into Bergerac’s tradition of thoughtful blending with a clear sense of place.

entries.heading: Quinta do Portal in the Douro
paragraphs: Quinta do Portal, a family‑owned wine estate anchored in the steep schist soils of Portugal’s Douro Valley, stands as both a historical and contemporary touchstone in the region. The estate dates back to at least the 15th century, with roots in the Douro demarcated region and experience in Port production that spans over a century ([thebft.co.uk](https://www.thebft.co.uk/images/PDFs/bft_2011.pdf?utm_source=openai)). Situated in the Cima‑Corgo sub‑region, Quinta do Portal benefits from diverse altitudes and exposures across its nearly 100 hectares of vineyard, including several parcels such as Quinta dos Muros and Quinta do Confradeiro ([provavanguarda.pt](https://www.provavanguarda.pt/uploads/products/attachments/pVeruEmzn8DDXdyL-960959QDP_Portal6Barrels_Tawny_Porto_PT.pdf?utm_source=openai)). These site-specific differences help produce balanced fruit ideal for both Port and Douro wines.

FineVines is proud to showcase the 2003 Vintage Port from Portal. This bottling exemplifies the estate’s understanding of both tradition and craft. As a Douro producer, Portal operates under the rigorous regulation and traceability frameworks administered by the Instituto dos Vinhos do Douro e do Porto (IVDP), ensuring that its wines reflect the authenticity and typicity of the Douro terroir ([digital.ivdp.pt](https://digital.ivdp.pt/en/?utm_source=openai)). The combination of ancestral viticulture, varied vineyards, and compliance with regional standards defines Portal’s Vintage Port as emblematic of the Douro’s unique character.

entries.name: Raposo
entries.heading: Carlos Raposo: A Singular Voice in Dão’s Touriga Nacional
paragraphs: Carlos Raposo is a native of the Dão region whose journey took him from Burgundy through Australia, Spain and the United States, before returning to craft low‑intervention wines rooted in his homeland. He sources small lots of Touriga Nacional (and other varieties) from cooler, granitic sites around Serra da Estrela, a terroir that shapes wines with mineral clarity and forest‑spice nuance. His philosophy is simple yet precise: respect the purity that nature grants each vintage and express it through restrained, authentic winemaking ([tourinto.pt](https://www.tourinto.pt/en/produtores-portugal/vinhos-do-dao/carlos-raposo/?utm_source=openai)).

The Dão region itself is an enclave in north‑central Portugal, nestled among mountain ranges such as Estrela, Buçaco, Caramulo and Nave, which shelter it from maritime and continental extremes. Vineyards thrive at elevations between 400 and 800 meters in predominantly granite soils, stimulating aromatic complexity, fine acidity and balance in both red and white wines. Touriga Nacional finds a congenial home here alongside varieties like Encruzado, Alfrocheiro and Jaen, helping define Dão’s elegant, ageworthy character ([ivv.gov.pt](https://www.ivv.gov.pt/np4/%7B%24clientServletPath%7D/?fileName=IVV_2024.pdf&newsId=1736&utm_source=openai)).

entries.heading: Discover Shibumi Knoll Vineyards
paragraphs: Shibumi Knoll is a boutique California wine producer founded in 2003 by Don and Joann Ross after purchasing a small knoll just north of St. Helena in Napa Valley. It included a .75‑acre Cabernet Sauvignon vineyard, a stone‑barn cottage, a guesthouse, and a modest winery, all of which has been carefully restored into their family home. The estate vineyard, planted in rocky soils and managed by David Abreu, produces Cabernet Sauvignon that speaks clearly of its unique terroir. The name Shibumi Knoll is inspired by the concept of “Shibumi,” a Japanese term meaning effortless perfection through simplicity([shibumiknoll.com](https://shibumiknoll.com/our-story/?utm_source=openai)).

Beyond the estate Cabernet, Shibumi Knoll is known for sourcing Chardonnay fruit from the historic Buena Tierra Vineyard in the Russian River Valley and Pinot Noir from Sonoma Coast sites, all vinified by Thomas Rivers Brown. These wines emphasize clarity, balance, and site expression. The Buena Tierra vines are more than 50 years old and were preserved thanks to Don’s early commitment to purchase their fruit. Thomas Rivers Brown’s guiding philosophy of minimal intervention allows the character of these vineyards to shine through in every release([napawineproject.com](https://www.napawineproject.com/shibumi-knoll-vineyards/?utm_source=openai)).

entries.heading: Sorelli’s Chianti from the Heart of Tuscany
paragraphs: Nestled in the rolling hills of central Tuscany, Sorelli is a family-owned wine estate with over a century devoted to Chianti and traditional regional expressions. Located in Figline e Incisa Valdarno near Florence, Vino Sorelli produces classic Chianti DOCG, Chianti Riserva, Superiore, Vin Santo, and Sangiovese IGT, combining modern production with deep ties to local growers and the Tuscan landscape ([consorziovinochianti.it](https://www.consorziovinochianti.it/aziende-old/vino-sorelli-s-p-a/?utm_source=openai)).

Chianti DOCG most often centers on Sangiovese, required to make up between 70 and 100 percent of the blend, while others such as Canaiolo, Colorino, and small percentages of Cabernet or white grapes may complement it ([consorziovinochianti.it](https://www.consorziovinochianti.it/chianti-identikit/?lang=en&utm_source=openai)). The style is typically vivid and dry, with savory tannins and floral or red fruit aromas that soften and gain complexity with age ([consorziovinochianti.it](https://www.consorziovinochianti.it/chianti-identikit/?lang=en&utm_source=openai)).

entries.heading: Sylvain Langoureau, Saint‑Aubin Chardonnay
paragraphs: Sylvain Langoureau is a fifth‑generation vigneron who assumed the family domaine in 1988. The estate today covers roughly ten hectares across appellations including Saint‑Aubin, Meursault, Chassagne‑Montrachet, and Puligny‑Montrachet, with a focus on Chardonnay. Farming is conducted with care and minimal intervention, and winemaking typically involves élevage in oak barrels with about twenty to thirty percent new oak over eleven months ([hachette-vins.com](https://www.hachette-vins.com/guide-vins/producteurs/9682/dom-sylvain-langoureau/?utm_source=openai)).

Saint‑Aubin, nestled between Puligny‑Montrachet and Chassagne‑Montrachet, is celebrated for its white wines, particularly from Premier Cru climats such as Les Frionnes and Sur le Sentier du Clou ([fr.wikipedia.org](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-aubin_%28AOC%29?utm_source=openai)). Langoureau’s Premier Cru Les Frionnes reflects this terroir’s mineral depth and freshness. Fermentation begins with native yeasts, and about twenty to thirty percent new oak is used, allowing the wine to retain tension and an expressive, crystalline clarity, suggestive of its limestone-rich site ([demainlesvins.com](https://www.demainlesvins.com/une-pepite-trop-meconnue-sur-saint-aubin-le-domaine-sylvain-langoureau-les-rares-2021/10983-domaine-sylvain-langoureau-saint-aubin-1er-cru-le-champlot-2016.html?utm_source=openai)).

entries.name: Terre Rouge
entries.heading: Terre Rouge: Rh ône Spirit from California’s Red Earth
paragraphs: Terre Rouge, founded in 1986 by winemaker Bill Easton and Jane O’Riordan in Amador County’s Sierra Foothills, built its reputation pioneering Rh ône varietals in this rugged and high‑altitude region. Bill Easton, one of the original members of the Rhône Rangers, helped elevate Syrah, Grenache, Mourvèdre, Viognier, Roussanne and Marsanne in this terroir of granite and volcanic soils. Their estate farming emphasizes sustainable and organic practices; the winery facility is solar‑powered and their vineyards are farmed with minimal environmental impact ([terrerougewines.com](https://www.terrerougewines.com/our-story?utm_source=openai)). The “Easton” label is reserved for non‑Rh ône varietals such as Zinfandel, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Barbera, further reflecting a thoughtful expression of regional adaptability ([terrerougewines.com](https://www.terrerougewines.com/our-story?utm_source=openai)).

FineVines carries a curated selection of Terre Rouge’s expressive bottlings drawn from Sierra Foothills appellations including Sierre, Shenandoah Valley and Clements Hills. These wines reflect the steep terrain and stony soils, offering structured yet graceful Syrahs, Mourvèdre‑based blends and GSM‑style expressions that evolve with age. As a wine professional, I encourage buyers to explore this portfolio not by vintage or inventory line‑item but by the common thread of terroir‑driven Rh ône tradition rendered in California’s “red earth.”

entries.name: Burgundy
entries.heading: Burgundy is a map of differences
paragraphs: Burgundy asks you to look closely. Its wines are organized around place, from broad regional appellations to villages and individual vineyard sites. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay do most of the work, but the story is not simply about grape variety. It is about how slope, exposure, soil, and generations of farming make neighboring parcels taste distinct.

Nowhere is that idea more visible than in the Climats of the Côte de Nuits and Côte de Beaune. UNESCO recognizes 1,247 precisely delimited vineyard parcels across a 50-kilometer strip south of Dijon. Stone walls, paths, and old boundaries still mark many of them. The FineVines Burgundy selection lets you move through that mosaic producer by producer and bottle by bottle.

entries.name: Liguria
entries.heading: Liguria’s Coastal Essence: Vermentino in the Riviera Ligure di Ponente
paragraphs: Liguria lies along Italy’s northwest coast and is among the country’s smallest wine regions. It is known for its steep, terraced slopes and challenging viticulture, often called heroic because growers work on nearly vertical terrain facing the sea ([impetodivino.it](https://www.impetodivino.it/vini/regioni/liguria?utm_source=openai)). Within Liguria, the Riviera Ligure di Ponente DOC stretches from the French border through the provinces of Imperia, Savona, and up into parts of Genoa. This broad and varied zone allows for notable variation in Vermentino styles, though each shares a coastal freshness and mineral imprint ([aisliguria.it](https://www.aisliguria.it/news/895-vermentino-ligure-conosci-a-quali-doc-appartiene-.html?PageSpeed=noscript&utm_source=openai)).

Vermentino is the white grape most closely linked with Liguria and especially this DOC. It thrives in poor, often calcareous soils, and benefits from maritime breezes that help retain acidity and aromatic intensity ([quattrocalici.it](https://www.quattrocalici.it/vitigni/vermentino/?utm_source=openai)). In Riviera Ligure di Ponente wines it must make up at least 95 percent of the blend. Expect a straw-yellow wine with delicate fruit and floral notes, a bright, sapid palate, and a clean, harmonious finish ([aisliguria.it](https://www.aisliguria.it/news/895-vermentino-ligure-conosci-a-quali-doc-appartiene-.html?PageSpeed=noscript&utm_source=openai)).

paragraphs: Rías Baixas is a Spanish Denominación de Origen located in Galicia’s northwest, primarily spanning the province of Pontevedra and parts of A Coruña. Its expression here reflects the maritime Atlantic climate, yielding wines with vibrant acidity, floral and stone‑fruit aromas, and a sense of drive and freshness ([museovinogalicia.xunta.gal](https://museovinogalicia.xunta.gal/es/el-vino/uvas-y-vinos-de-galicia/albarino?utm_source=openai)). Albariño reaches its fullest sense of place in Rías Baixas, where rainfall, moderating temperatures, and mineral soils combine to highlight the grape’s clarity and regional character ([riasbaixaswines.com](https://www.riasbaixaswines.com/?utm_source=openai)).

entries.name: Chardonnay
entries.heading: Understanding Chardonnay: Versatile and Terroir‑Driven
paragraphs: Chardonnay originated in Burgundy, France, where it remains the flagship white varietal. Its neutral flavor profile allows terroir and winemaking to shape every bottle, resulting in expressions ranging from the steely, mineral‑driven wines of Chablis to the richer, subtly oaked whites of the Côte de Beaune. In cooler Burgundian sites, Chardonnay often exhibits bright citrus, green apple, and flinty notes with elegant acidity; in warmer locales or through oak influence, expect layered stone fruit, hazelnut, and cream‑accented nuance. These stylistic shifts emerge from its sensitivity to soil, exposure, climate, and technique, making Chardonnay a superb interpreter of place. ([bourgogne-wines.com](https://www.bourgogne-wines.com/wine-and-terroir/our-grape-varietals-our-colors/chardonnay/chardonnay-a-bourgogne-original-that-has-travelled-the-world%2C2797%2C10602.html?utm_source=openai))

Beyond France, Chardonnay’s adaptability has made it a fixture in winemaking regions worldwide. In California it is the most planted white variety, where winemakers have historically favored fuller‑bodied, oak‑influenced styles featuring ripe fruit, vanilla, and creamy textures. More recently, many producers have pivoted toward leaner, fresher expressions with subtler oak to preserve fruit brightness. This tempering of the once‑ubiquitous buttery style reflects broader shifts toward balance and site expression. ([wineinstitute.org](https://wineinstitute.org/our-industry/statistics/wine-fact-sheets/chardonnay/?utm_source=openai))

entries.name: Chasselas Dore
entries.heading: Chasselas Doré in the Willamette Valley
paragraphs: Chasselas Doré is a venerable white grape variety rooted in central Europe and Switzerland, where it has been cultivated for centuries. Recognized under the official name “Chasselas doré” by U.S. regulatory standards, it also goes by many synonyms including Gutedel and Golden Chasselas ([fps.ucdavis.edu](https://fps.ucdavis.edu/FGRfamilies.cfm?varietyid=443&utm_source=openai)). In its ancestral terroirs, the variety is known for delicate, refined fruit and gentle floral notes, frequently picked early for its brightness.

At Eyrie Vineyards in Oregon’s Dundee Hills, this rare grape has found a congenial home. Planted on their organic, ungrafted Sisters Vineyard, the vines embody the estate’s regenerative, low-intervention ethic ([eyrievineyards.com](https://eyrievineyards.com/pdfs/download/23CHASSE.pdf?utm_source=openai)). The wine is crafted with natural fermentations and extended lees contact, yielding a wine of low alcohol yet noteworthy structure and texture. The resulting expression is fresh and savory, with suggestions of melon, floral hints, and a softly tactile finish that makes it a quietly intriguing choice in FineVines’ catalog.

entries.name: Fernao Pires / Baga
entries.heading: Fernao Pires and Baga in Bairrada: Aromatic Contrast from a Coastal Terroir
paragraphs: Fernao Pires is one of Portugal's most widely planted white grape varieties and is especially associated with central regions such as Tejo and Bairrada, where it is also known locally as Maria Gomes. It produces highly aromatic wines, often with floral, citrus, or exotic fruit notes, and is valued for its versatility, from bright, youthful whites to delicate sparkling styles. The grape has early budding and ripening tendencies, which means that timing of harvest is crucial to preserve its freshness. INIAV notes it is agronomically significant in the white varietal landscape and widely planted across central and southern Portugal ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fern%C3%A3o_Pires?utm_source=openai)).

Baga, by contrast, is the red grape queen of Bairrada. Thriving in the region's clay-limestone soils with maritime influence and wide diurnal temperature swings, Baga delivers wines rich in color, brimming in tannin and known for their persistence. The Bairrada Denomination of Origin describes it as central to the region's identity and a source of structure and longevity in red wines. The region benefits from cool Atlantic breezes that help retain acidity even under hot summer conditions ([cvbairrada.pt](https://www.cvbairrada.pt/en/regiao-1500/?utm_source=openai)).

entries.name: Macabeo / Garnacha
entries.heading: Macabeo Alongside Garnacha in Penedès
paragraphs: In Penedès, Macabeo (also known regionally as Macabeu or Viura) is a foundational white grape, valued for its versatility across dry still wines and sparkling styles such as Cava. Indigenous to Catalonia and often blended with Xarel·lo and Parellada, it yields fresh and floral expressions when vinified in stainless steel and subtly fuller, nutty character when allowed oak exposure. It remains cherished for its moderate acidity and strong ageing potential despite modest aromatic intensity ([cava.wine](https://www.cava.wine/es/origen/variedades-de-uva-autorizadas/?utm_source=openai)).

Garnacha, a red variety with deep roots in eastern Spain, contributes weight and ripe red fruit tones when paired with Macabeo, especially in rosé and light red blends. In Penedès, Garnacha Negra is a permitted red variety under the DOP and is sometimes used in blending across still and sparkling offerings. The combination of Macabeo’s structure with Garnacha’s warmth offers a pleasing balance when crafting fresh, approachable rosés or lighter reds ([dopenedes.cat](https://dopenedes.cat/en/dopenedes/?utm_source=openai)).

entries.name: Prieto Picudo
entries.heading: Prieto Picudo from León: aromatic intensity meets freshness
paragraphs: Prieto Picudo is a red grape variety native to the southern part of the province of León in Castile‑and‑León, Spain. It is the principal grape of the Tierra de León Denominación de Origen, covering roughly two‑thirds of the region’s vineyard area ([es.wikipedia.org](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prieto_picudo?utm_source=openai)). The name refers to its dense, compact clusters (“prieto”) and the pointed, oval berries (“picudo”) ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prieto_Picudo?utm_source=openai)). Traditionally cultivated as low‑trained, sprawling vines to protect against frost, modern plantings increasingly use trellised systems to improve vineyard management ([bodegasvinosdeleon.es](https://www.bodegasvinosdeleon.es/variedades?utm_source=openai)). Agronomically, Prieto Picudo is drought‑resistant, moderately fertile, and well adapted to high summer heat and UV exposure ([bodegasvinosdeleon.es](https://www.bodegasvinosdeleon.es/variedades?utm_source=openai)).

Wines from Prieto Picudo are notable for their aromatic clarity, lively natural acidity (often around 7 g/l tartaric acid), and deep pigmentation due to thick skins rich in polyphenols ([doleon.es](https://www.doleon.es/en/history/varieties-of-grape-and-wine/?utm_source=openai)). It has long been used to make “rosados de aguja” via the traditional “madreo” method, in which whole grapes are added during fermentation, adding freshness and aromatic lift ([doleon.es](https://www.doleon.es/en/history/varieties-of-grape-and-wine/?utm_source=openai)). The variety also excels in red wine production, yielding intensely aromatic, persistent wines with good structure and balance, whether young or lightly aged ([bodegasvinosdeleon.es](https://www.bodegasvinosdeleon.es/variedades?utm_source=openai)).

entries.name: Sercial / Maria Gomes
entries.heading: Sercial / Maria Gomes in Bairrada
paragraphs: The Bairrada region in Portugal is a coastal Denominação de Origem Controlada renowned for its blend of clay‑limestone and sandy soils and its Atlantic‑moderated climate, which yield distinctive whites and sparkling wines marked by freshness and nuance. Anaerobic conditions and foggy influence create vibrant styles, with whites often fragrant and balanced. Bairrada is a vital component of the broader Beira Atlântico indication, regulated by bodies such as the Comissão Vitivinícola da Bairrada and the Instituto da Vinha e do Vinho ([pt.wikipedia.org](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bairrada_DOC?utm_source=openai)).

The Maria Gomes grape, also known elsewhere as Fernão Pires, is the most widely planted white variety in Bairrada. It thrives in sandy soils and under the Atlantic breeze, producing expressive wines with citrus and floral aromas, sustaining natural acidity and aromatic intensity especially when handled with care in vineyard and cellar. Sercial or Sercialinho appears occasionally alongside it, typically in blends, though in Bairrada it is not itself a dominant or standalone component and its identity is more associated with Madeira rather than this region ([heldercunha.com](https://heldercunha.com/castas-autoctones-da-bairrada-doc/?utm_source=openai)).

entries.name: Syrah / Grenache
entries.heading: Syrah and Grenache: a classic Rhône blend with modern expression
paragraphs: Syrah and Grenache are two of the Rhône Valley’s signature red varieties, often blended to marry structure and warmth. Syrah contributes deep color, peppery spice, darker fruit and firm tannins, while Grenache brings red fruit charm, softness, and fragrant warmth. That synergy underpins the southern Rhône tradition, where Grenache typically plays the dominant role, balanced by Syrah’s backbone for shape and length ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah?utm_source=openai)).

In Israel’s Upper Galilee, Galil Mountain Winery includes Syrah and Grenache together in its flagship blends. The high-elevation vineyards deliver both elegance and ripeness, and their intentional blend echoes Rhône sensibilities with a local voice rooted in terroir ([galilmountain.co.il](https://www.galilmountain.co.il/en/home/a/main/?utm_source=openai)). This collection invites exploration of FineVines offerings from both Galil Mountain and the Rhône, allowing buyers to compare how the same grape pairing can express its character across different soils, climates and winemaking philosophies.

entries.name: Torrontes/sb/chardonnay
entries.heading: A Fresh Trio from Mendoza: Torrontés, Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay
paragraphs: This blend brings together three white grape varieties that each contribute their own voice to a carefully balanced ensemble. Torrontés is Argentina’s singularly native white grape, a cross of Muscat of Alexandria and Criolla Chica that yields intensely floral, fresh wines with characteristic notes of jasmine, rose petal, and white peach supported by brisk acidity ([vinosargentinos.com](https://www.vinosargentinos.com/argentine-grape-varieties/torrontes-grape?utm_source=openai)). Sauvignon Blanc adds vibrant citrus, herbaceous clarity, and racy energy. Chardonnay lends structure and a supple mid-palate, its neutral profile providing support to the aromatic cast. The combination creates a wine that is aromatic yet structured, lively yet grounded, ideal for capturing the brightness of Mendoza’s white-wine potential.

Mendoza provides a generous viticultural canvas for this blend. Though Torrontés reaches its most expressive heights in the high-altitude valleys of Salta, Mendoza delivers a riper, fruit-forward take that plays well in blends ([vinosargentinos.com](https://www.vinosargentinos.com/argentine-grape-varieties/torrontes-grape?utm_source=openai)). The region’s continental climate, with its sunny days and cool nights, helps preserve acidity while concentrating flavor in all three varieties. This makes Mendoza an excellent setting for crafting a versatile white blend that delivers aromatic interest, weight, and freshness all in one glass.
